Subject: Three things worth doing on trail this autumn
CTA: Find your local trail association -> https://www.northbaysupply.com/trail-care-resources
Body: Hey,

Autumn is a good time to slow down and pay a little more attention to the trail beneath your boots. Here are three specific habits worth building into your fall outings.

---

**1. Step in the mud, not around it.**
When the trail gets wet and muddy, the instinct is to walk along the edges. Resist it. Widening a trail — even by half a step — accelerates erosion and degrades the root systems of trailside vegetation. Muddy boots clean up. Damaged trail edges take years to recover.

---

**2. Clear water bars before the ground freezes.**
Water bars — those diagonal drainage channels cut across the tread — get packed with leaf litter fast in October and November. A clogged water bar sends runoff down the trail instead of off it, which cuts ruts through winter and into spring. If you're carrying a trekking pole or a sturdy stick, a few seconds of clearing as you hike makes a real difference. Many trail crews ask hikers to do exactly this.

---

**3. Report blowdowns promptly.**
Fall windstorms drop trees across trails faster than crews can patrol. Most land managers — national forests, state parks, local trail associations — have an online reporting form or a ranger district phone line. A quick note with a location (GPS coordinates or a trail-mile marker if you have it) helps crews prioritize cuts before the trail gets rerouted around a log and a second problem starts.

---

These aren't complicated. They're just easy to skip when you're tired and focused on the descent. Worth adding to the routine.

See you out there,
Northbay Supply
